newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Crystallex ruling not final decision.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Crystallex ruling not final decision.

text.p: A recent ruling by Venezuela's Supreme Court in favor of Crystallex International Corp does not resolve its legal battle for the gold rich Las Cristinas concession, but the company remains optimistic, a Crystallex spokesman said.
Further rulings by the Supreme Court are required before the case can be finally settled either way, Crystallex Vice President Richard Marshall told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"We understand that the courts should proceeed fairly quickly ... We're looking forward to their decision," he said.

Crystallex stock has soared in recent days on market rumors that the Supreme Court's April 15 ruling was a definite decision in the legal clash that has pitched Crystallex against the Republic of Venezuela and Placer Dome Inc over Las Cristinas.
Crystallex says the Las Cristinas concessions are its own by right after it bought local company Inversores Mael in late 1996.
The April 15 Supreme Court rulings, published last Thursday in Venezuela's Gazette which records official legislation, confirm that Mael once owned the concessions.
But Marshall said the rulings do not deal with Mael's 1989 attempt to renew its rights to the concessions, which the Ministry of Mines extinguished later the same year.
"We have a motion pending ... (that) deals with the reversal of the denial of the renewal of the concession," he said. "We're getting there inch by inch."
Marshall added that a waiver in 1991 by Mael for the concessions did not prejudice Crystallex's claim.
"Mael only agreed not to sue ... the agreement did not prejudice its claim for the concessions," he said.

Placer has flatly rejected Crystalex's argument that it should rightly have control of the concessions. Venezuelan government officials and the CVG, the Venezuelan state-owned company that is a 30 percent partner with Placer in the Cristinas project, have sided with Placer.
The dispute has delayed the start of construction of a $576 million mine at the site.
